items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Saturday night, the 26th of April I played this session with Dicky Wells, Eddie Barefield, the great Willie "the Lion" Smith and two drummers, Jo Jones and Panama Francis.

ctx.x: few with him. There are many name musicians in the 20s and 30s that gigged at one time with Fernand; Benny Carter, Rex Stewart, Bobby Starke, etc. When I gigged with Fernand, I met one of the greatest alto sax men in the business. His name was Hilton Jefferson. Jeff was a very quiet man but he made his horn talk for him and all the musicians loved him.

Another musician that always had the highest paid gigs was a drummer named Peek-a-Boo Jimmy. Peek-a-Boo had played with James P. Johnson, Willie 'The Lion' Smith and 'Lucky' Roberts in the days before I even dreamed of going to New York. I gigged with Peek-a-Boo twice and both times it was really enjoyable. The music we played was not very jazzy because Jimmy was a drummer who had lost sight of what the other drummers were doing. And most of the musicians he hired were a certain age and not up to date on jazz…

But Jimmy was in with the rich folks downtown and he played many high society functions. The first one I did with him was a stag party for some business men who had rented a Hudson River cruising boat and invited about 400 men to cruise up the Hudson. We played but there was no dancing as there were no women to dance with. Finally we docked somewhere and everybody went ashore where a big picnic with all kinds of seafood and kegs of beer were waiting for everyone including the band. The committee of this outing…

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The first of December, Buck Clayton and George Johnson along with the "Lion" ... were invited to the session. ... The 'Lion' was real groovie and we all had that New York jam session feeling

ctx.x: Other than the fact that we had no music on the stands, we still made a hit with the public at the Chikito. Later Norman Lester wrote some original tunes which actually had no swing possibilities and although he was a good piano man, he was not an arranger. But we played the tunes every night because I was a begger and had no choice.

"Willie the Lion" Smith came to Europe during this time and his tour brought him to Berne. There was a jam session every Saturday and Sunday afternoon at which I would invite the local musicians to participate and the joint would jump during these sessions. The first of December, Buck Clayton and George Johnson along with the "Lion" (who was giving recitals in Switzerland at the time), were invited to the session. Merrill Spepter was also there because Buck was engaged to play a ball in a hotel that night with a…

I taken the occasion to ask "Buck" if he would make me some arrangements, but for some reason which I never found out why, he never did any for me and he was engaged through the influence of Felix to come to the Chikito quite a few times and play with my orchestra.
